comments.note: PageHeaderView.axaml.cs: The constructor calls App.Services.GetRequiredService<INavigationService>() at construction time. If PageHeaderView is ever instantiated in a context where App.Services is not yet initialised (e.g., the Avalonia designer or early unit tests), this will throw InvalidOperationException. A test bootstrap that sets App.Services before creating the view is required.

PageHeaderView.axaml.cs: BackCommand is an ICommand? StyledProperty. If no BackCommand is set and the BreadcrumbBar item is clicked, the null-check (`BackCommand is not null`) allows navigation to proceed. If callers want to always-guard breadcrumb navigation, they must supply a BackCommand. This is intentional but should be documented in QA tests.

PageHeaderView.axaml.cs: IsTitleVisible is initialised to false (field default) and is only updated in OnPropertyChanged when TitleProperty changes. If TitleProperty is never set after construction (stays at default string.Empty), the TextBlock remains hidden. This is the correct behaviour per AC4.

summary: Reviewed PageHeaderView.axaml (AXAML layout + compiled bindings), PageHeaderView.axaml.cs (Avalonia UserControl with StyledProperties and DirectProperties), PageHeaderViewTests.cs (13 AvaloniaFact tests), and manifest updates.

All five AC are met: build is clean, IsBackVisible mirrors CanGoBack and reacts to NavigationChanged, BackCommand disables both the Back button and breadcrumb click handler, TitleProperty correctly gates IsTitleVisible via IsNullOrEmpty, and INavigationService is resolved from App.Services with no StyledProperty.
The AXAML uses compiled bindings (x:DataType=local:PageHeaderView) and the BreadcrumbBar DataTemplate also uses compiled bindings (x:DataType=nav:BreadcrumbItem), consistent with project constraints.
Constructor correctly initialises backing fields before InitializeComponent(), ensuring DirectProperty bindings read correct initial values. Unloaded unsubscription prevents memory leaks.
The whitespace-only Title behaviour (IsTitleVisible=true for whitespace, per IsNullOrEmpty) is intentional per spec and documented by QA test.
No Blocking issues. No Fix-Forward changes. One Documentation-Forward item tagged (BackCommandProperty null vs CanExecute=false semantics).

comments.note: PageHeaderView.axaml.cs: The OnBreadcrumbItemClicked guard `if (BackCommand is not null && !BackCommand.CanExecute(null)) return;` is correct. When BackCommand is null (default), the guard does not block navigation — breadcrumb clicks always navigate. When BackCommand is set with CanExecute=false, both the button (via Avalonia command binding) and the breadcrumb handler are suppressed. This is the intended two-path disable behaviour described by the AC.

PageHeaderView.axaml: The 3-column Grid uses ColumnDefinitions='*,Auto,*'. The left (*) and right (*) columns are equal weight, which correctly centres the optional title TextBlock in column 1 when both side panels have equal content. If the left StackPanel (breadcrumb) grows significantly wider than the right, the title will appear off-centre visually. This is a layout trade-off acceptable for the current scope.

[documentation-forward] PageHeaderView.axaml.cs: The BackCommandProperty semantics are non-obvious: null means do not block breadcrumb navigation; non-null with CanExecute=false means suppress both the Back button and breadcrumb navigation. A brief XML doc comment on the BackCommandProperty static field (or the CLR wrapper) clarifying this duality would prevent misuse.

summary: Added XML doc comment block to BackCommandProperty in PageHeaderView.axaml.cs. The <remarks> section documents the two-path disable behaviour: null leaves breadcrumb navigation unblocked; a non-null command with CanExecute=false suppresses both the Back button (via Avalonia command binding) and the breadcrumb ItemClicked handler.
Documentation-forward from the code-review pipeline fully addressed.
